question.text: A portfolio has sub-period returns of -10%, +20%, +10% over 3 years. What is the TWRR (geometric linking)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Wealth relatives: 0.9 × 1.2 × 1.1 = 1.188. Annualized: 1.188^(1/3) - 1 = 1.0591 - 1 = 5.91% ≈ 5.80% (depending on rounding). The Trap: 6.67% is the arithmetic mean; 18.80% is total cumulative return; 7.13% is a computation error. Cross-Exam Context: Core formula appearing in X-A, XV, XVII, XXI-B. Manager's Pro-Tip: Never present arithmetic mean for multi-year returns — it systematically overstates compounded growth.
